headline: Your AI agent can pay for anything now. That's the problem.
summary: A new protocol, x402, enables AI agents to make instant stablecoin payments, but it lacks built-in identity or trust mechanisms. This leaves developers responsible for vetting counterparties, a critical challenge at machine speed.
details: AI agents can now autonomously pay for services using x402, an HTTP 402 protocol extension. This allows instant stablecoin transactions without human intervention, completing in about one second.

The x402 protocol has seen rapid adoption, with over 165 million transactions by mid-2026 across 69,000 active agents. Major players like Coinbase, Cloudflare, and Google are involved, proving the rail's speed and viability.

However, x402 intentionally lacks identity, reputation, or trust mechanisms, leaving this responsibility to developers. While this design choice aided adoption, it creates a significant vulnerability for autonomous agents.

Unlike humans who can detect and react to fraudulent transactions, AI agents simply pay and move on, lacking shared memory of failures. This oversight can lead to repeated payments to malicious endpoints at machine speed and scale.

A 2026 study on the ERC-8004 agent ecosystem revealed that up to 86.8% of "rated" agents had no valid feedback, with 59-91% of reviewers exhibiting Sybil behavior. This indicates a widespread issue with the trustworthiness of on-chain reputation systems.

The problem is structural: generating fake reviews is significantly cheaper than earning genuine ones. Even pre-authorization mechanisms fail, as colluding agents can easily mint mutual praise for minimal cost.

While settlement (x402) and identity (ERC-8004) for agents are largely solved, the crucial aspect of counterparty trust remains unaddressed. Knowing an agent's identity doesn't guarantee its trustworthiness in transactions.

The agentic economy has built excellent "passports" but lacks a robust "credit rating" system. This leaves agents vulnerable, as they effectively extend credit based solely on identity without assessing trustworthiness.

headline: Elon Musk's AI Wikipedia, Grokipedia, hasn't been updated in months, report finds
summary: xAI's Grokipedia, once touted as a 'massive improvement' over Wikipedia, reportedly hasn't processed any suggested edits or updated its content since April 24th.
details: xAI's Grokipedia, an online encyclopedia Elon Musk once promised would be a 'massive improvement' over Wikipedia, reportedly hasn't been updated since April 24th. Lawfare's report notes that 'no entry has changed in more than three months'.

Grokipedia launched in October 2025 (v0.1) and is now on v0.2 (November 2025) with over 6 million articles. However, its 'Recent changes' section on grokipedia.com/live currently states, 'No live edits available right now'.
Lawfare analyzed 34,519 pages with 225,496 suggested edits and found no accepted or rejected corrections dated within the past three months. This suggests a complete halt in content moderation.
xAI has not responded to requests for comment regarding the inactivity. Users on Reddit and X are questioning if Grokipedia is 'dead,' and Musk's last X post mentioning the project was in February.
caption:
Elon Musk's AI-powered encyclopedia, Grokipedia, has reportedly not been updated in over three months.

xAI's Grokipedia, an online encyclopedia Elon Musk once promised would be a 'massive improvement' over Wikipedia, reportedly hasn't been updated since April 24th. Lawfare's report notes that 'no entry has changed in more than three months'.

Grokipedia launched in October 2025 (v0.1) and is now on v0.2 (November 2025) with over 6 million articles. However, its 'Recent changes' section on grokipedia.com/live currently states, 'No live edits available right now'.

Lawfare analyzed 34,519 pages with 225,496 suggested edits and found no accepted or rejected corrections dated within the past three months. This suggests a complete halt in content moderation.

xAI has not responded to requests for comment regarding the inactivity. Users on Reddit and X are questioning if Grokipedia is 'dead,' and Musk's last X post mentioning the project was in February.
